title: ChatGPT export memory and RAG system
description: Build a private local memory layer from exported ChatGPT logs. The system should preserve raw exports, normalize conversations, support keyword and semantic retrieval, expose subject/project browsing, and provide agent-safe tiered memory disclosure.
design: Use multiple memory systems instead of one monolithic store: immutable raw archive, normalized searchable archive, semantic chunk index, curated working memory, and agent-facing retrieval tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Roadmap beads exist for ingestion, storage, FTS search, embeddings, hybrid ranking, curated memory, subject browsing, privacy controls, and evals.

title: Define ChatGPT memory schemas and folder contracts
description: Define the on-disk and SQLite contracts for ChatGPT exports before ingestion code lands. Cover raw exports, parsed conversations, chunks, embeddings, curated memories, source links, subjects, and retrieval events.
design: Use immutable raw files under data/chatgpt_exports/raw, normalized JSONL under data/chatgpt_exports/parsed, and SQLite tables for conversations, messages, chunks, memory_records, subjects, embeddings metadata, and retrieval logs.
acceptance_criteria: A spec or design doc defines directories, table names, required fields, indexes, IDs, and migration expectations for the ChatGPT memory system.

title: Implement ChatGPT export ingestion
description: Add a CLI ingestion path for exported ChatGPT data. Parse supported export files into stable conversation, message, and attachment metadata records without modifying the original export.
design: Start with the standard ChatGPT export conversations.json shape. Add parser boundaries so additional export variants can be supported later. Keep raw files immutable and write normalized JSONL plus SQLite records.
acceptance_criteria: lagent ingest-chatgpt --input data/chatgpt_exports/raw imports conversations, preserves source file references, reports counts, is idempotent when run twice, supports --dry-run --trace, writes import_report.json and trace.jsonl under data/logs/<run_id>/, and localizes parse/write errors to stage plus source file or record ID.

title: Build keyword archive search over ChatGPT logs
description: Add fast exact and keyword search over imported ChatGPT conversations so agents and humans can find known phrases, project names, workflows, dates, and titles.
design: Use SQLite FTS5 first. Search should return conversation title, timestamp, role, snippet, source conversation ID, and enough metadata to inspect the original context.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-search "query" returns ranked FTS hits with citations to conversation/message/chunk IDs, supports basic filters for subject, date range, and conversation title, and supports --explain --json with candidate counts, filters, score breakdowns, source kinds, disclosure tiers, and run_id.

title: Add semantic embeddings for conversation chunks
description: Generate and store local embeddings for imported ChatGPT conversation chunks so memory search can find related context even when the query uses different wording.
design: Use the configured local embeddings profile first, likely nomic-embed-text through Ollama. Store embedding metadata in SQLite and keep the vector backend swappable between a simple local store, sqlite-vss, or Qdrant later.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-embed builds embeddings for imported chunks, skips unchanged chunks, records model/version metadata, and exposes clear status when the embedding backend is unavailable.

title: Implement hybrid memory ranking and tiered disclosure
description: Combine keyword relevance, semantic similarity, recency, subject match, and curated memory trust into one inspectable retrieval path. Expose more context only as semantic closeness increases.
design: Use disclosure tiers: far matches expose title/date/one-line summary; medium matches expose relevant chunks; close matches expose surrounding turns and extracted decisions; very close matches expose a wider conversation window and related curated memories.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-search can return a hybrid-ranked result set with explainable scores and a --depth option controlling far, medium, close, and full disclosure.

title: Add curated working memory records
description: Create an explicit, editable memory layer for durable facts agents should trust more than raw chat transcripts. Support project facts, decisions, user preferences, workflows, open loops, and lessons learned.
design: Keep curated memory separate from raw logs. Store records in SQLite with optional Markdown/YAML export so users can inspect and edit them. Promotion should be deliberate, not automatic by default.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-promote can convert a search result or chunk into a typed memory record, lagent memory-show displays it with provenance, and promoted records are included in ranked retrieval.

title: Add subject, project, and workflow browsing
description: Let users and agents browse imported ChatGPT memory by subject, project, workflow type, and time period instead of only searching by query.
design: Start with explicit metadata and lightweight inferred tags. Later clustering can suggest subjects, but user-editable labels should remain authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-subjects lists subjects with counts and recency, lagent memory-search supports subject filters, and imported conversations can be assigned or corrected by subject.

title: Expose agent-facing memory context commands
description: Provide commands local agents can call to retrieve relevant ChatGPT memory with controlled depth and clear provenance.
design: Keep the interface CLI-first before adding daemons or APIs. Output should support Markdown for humans and JSON for agents, with citations back to conversation/chunk/memory IDs.
acceptance_criteria: lagent memory-context "query" returns ranked context packs with provenance, depth controls, source type labels, and enough metadata for agents to decide whether to inspect more.

title: Add privacy controls and memory audit trail
description: Protect personal ChatGPT exports by default. Track ingestion, retrieval, promotion, and deletion events, and make it clear what content was exposed to an agent.
design: Use local-only defaults, redaction before model calls, immutable raw export provenance, deletions/tombstones for records, and inspectable retrieval logs. Do not send personal memory to external APIs unless explicitly configured.
acceptance_criteria: Memory commands label source types, log retrieval events, support blocking/excluding conversations or subjects, strip obvious secrets before model calls, can show what context was exposed for a run, and integrate with lagent memory-trace <run-id>.

title: Create ChatGPT memory eval fixtures and quality checks
description: Add test fixtures and measurable checks for the memory system so retrieval quality and privacy behavior do not regress as ranking gets smarter.
design: Use synthetic exported conversations covering multiple projects and workflows. Evaluate exact search, semantic recall, subject filtering, tiered disclosure, provenance, and redaction.
acceptance_criteria: python -m pytest covers ingestion/search/ranking behavior, and a lagent memory-eval command or fixture runner reports pass/fail checks for known queries, trace artifacts, memory-check integrity failures, disclosure tiers, provenance, and redaction.

title: Document memory modes and operating model
description: Write the user-facing operating model for the multiple memory systems: raw archive, keyword search, semantic memory, curated working memory, and agent context packs.
design: Document when each memory type should be used, what agents can trust, what remains user-editable, and how disclosure depth changes with semantic closeness.
acceptance_criteria: README or spec docs explain the memory modes, commands, storage locations, privacy defaults, and recommended workflows for project-specific memory browsing.

title: Add memory observability and verification harness
description: Make the ChatGPT memory system inspectable from the terminal before and during implementation. Add trace-first CLI behavior, validation commands, run artifacts, and failure localization so ingestion/search/ranking are not black boxes.
design: Every memory command should emit a run_id, JSON artifacts under data/logs/<run_id>/, and audit rows where relevant. Add dry-run and --trace modes for ingestion, --explain JSON for search/ranking, memory-check for integrity validation, and memory-trace for replaying what happened in a run.
acceptance_criteria: Beads and docs require lagent ingest-chatgpt --dry-run --trace, lagent memory-check, lagent memory-search --explain --json, and lagent memory-trace <run-id>. The contract defines required trace artifacts, validation checks, failure categories, and how errors point to file/record/stage.

title: Catch up the full-history adaptive memory spec
description: Deliver the remaining work needed to turn the full ChatGPT-history memory spec into an implementable local memory substrate. The goal is a staged, inspectable, local-first memory system that can ingest exports, extract candidate memories, retrieve by domain and lens, and evolve through feedback.
design: Treat the spec as Stage 1.5 to Stage 2: lock the ontology first, then implement candidate memory extraction, domain-scoped retrieval, effort-based disclosure, active memory lifecycle, high-risk governance, and end-to-end validation. First release defaults stay conservative; later releases can widen allowances only after the underlying system is proven.
acceptance_criteria: Beads exist for the memory ontology, candidate extraction, scoped retrieval, lens/effort tiers, active memory lifecycle, risk governance, observability, and evals. Each bead has a clear blocking order so implementation can proceed without re-litigating scope. First release behavior remains locked down and conservative by default.

title: Lock the canonical memory ontology and provenance model
description: Define the canonical memory types, reason types, domain list, lens list, temporal validity fields, and provenance rules that all downstream extraction and retrieval code will use.
design: Make the spec executable by pinning the schema for memory records, source links, domain labels, assistant-vs-user provenance, and validity states before extraction logic expands any further. Domain detection may use model assistance, but the canonical labels and policy outputs remain explicit and inspectable.
acceptance_criteria: The repo defines one canonical ontology for domains, memory types, reason types, lenses, and validity states. Assistant suggestions remain distinguishable from user-confirmed memories, and every durable memory has traceable source links and status semantics. Model-assisted domain detection is supported, but its outputs are constrained to the canonical domain set.

title: Extract candidate memories from full ChatGPT history
description: Turn raw ChatGPT exports into reviewable candidate memories with source links, memory types, reason types, domain tags, confidence, and temporal validity metadata.
design: Build the Stage 1.5 ingestion layer that reads transcript history, separates assistant suggestions from user-confirmed outcomes, and emits structured candidates instead of pretending the raw archive is already memory. Assistant suggestions stay in a separate, lower-trust candidate tier until the user explicitly confirms them.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion can produce candidate memories for episodes, facts, preferences, procedures, failures, decisions, open loops, and risks, all linked back to source conversations/messages/chunks. Candidate records are reviewable and do not overwrite the raw archive. Assistant-only suggestions remain segregated from confirmed memory until later-release policies change.

title: Implement domain detection and scoped retrieval
description: Detect the query domain, prefer matching domains, and expand to adjacent domains only under explicit rules. Cross-domain results must be labeled as analogies or transfer, not literal fact.
design: Replace loose subject browsing with a real domain-scoping policy that can steer retrieval across cooking, lab automation, career, finance, health, relationships, and the other initial domains without uncontrolled drift. Use model assistance for domain detection, but keep the final domain labels and expansion rules explicit, bounded, and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Search/context requests choose primary domains, expand only when allowed by effort or explicit request, and label cross-domain results clearly. Domain drift is prevented by policy rather than left to embeddings alone. Model-assisted domain detection is allowed, but outputs must map to the canonical domain list.

title: Add effort tiers, lenses, and contradiction checks
description: Make retrieval choose different depth, lens, and validation behavior at effort levels 1 through 5. The system should expose more context only when the query warrants it.
design: Translate the spec's reflex/basic/structured/deep/exploratory model into concrete retrieval behavior, including graph traversal, temporal checks, contradiction checks, and disclosure expansion.
acceptance_criteria: Retrieval supports explicit effort levels, lens selection, contradiction and temporal checks at higher effort, and explainable disclosure changes from far to full. Higher effort returns more context only when the policy allows it.

title: Implement active memory lifecycle and feedback
description: Add reinforcement, decay, open-loop tracking, and feedback-driven status changes so memory quality improves with use instead of staying static.
design: Store retrieval feedback, source preferences, and freshness signals locally. Use them to reinforce good paths, weaken misleading ones, and surface unresolved open loops for later review.
acceptance_criteria: The system can record positive and negative feedback, update memory status over time, and reflect repeated usefulness or repeated failure in retrieval behavior. Open loops can be promoted, resolved, or deprecated explicitly.

title: Add governance for high-risk domains
description: Treat health, finance, relationships, and similar domains as special cases with stricter temporal validity, source authority, and skepticism rules.
design: Encode the spec's caution layers so high-risk retrieval gets stricter validation, explicit uncertainty, and narrower disclosure than ordinary browsing or recall. Default allowances should stay tightened in the first release and only expand later after the base system proves itself.
acceptance_criteria: High-risk queries are flagged, use stricter source and freshness checks, and never let old or assistant-only suggestions masquerade as current advice or fact. Skeptic review is explicit rather than implied. First-release defaults remain conservative across all allowance knobs.

title: Expand observability and evaluation for the new memory stages
description: Make the new extraction, retrieval, feedback, and governance stages inspectable from the terminal with trace artifacts, validation checks, and regression fixtures.
design: Extend the existing trace-first model to every new memory stage so failures point to a stage, record, source, or policy decision instead of showing up as a black box.
acceptance_criteria: New commands or stages emit run artifacts, trace events, and validation output. The eval suite covers domain drift, assistant-vs-user separation, temporal supersession, disclosure tiers, high-risk governance cases, and conservative first-release defaults.

title: Home MCP for Mac mini
description: Build a self-hosted MCP server on the Mac mini that gives ChatGPT and Codex narrow, auditable access to approved home/project directories and a basic recipe book directory. Start with safe read-only file discovery plus create-only/append-only Markdown note tools, then add remote access plumbing and later expand into memory-backed recipe and household workflows.
design: Treat the Mac mini as the controlled host for external AI clients. The MVP should expose only allowlisted roots, no arbitrary shell, no deletes, and no unrestricted filesystem browsing. Recipe content should land in a simple local recipe book directory first, with hardcoded/structured note-like files that can later be surfaced through the memory system.
acceptance_criteria: A separate epic exists for the Mac mini MCP surface. Child beads define allowlisted roots, path safety, read/search tools, create-only note/recipe write tools, audit logging, and remote access transport. The first release keeps the surface narrow and reversible, and recipe content can be stored locally in a basic recipe book directory for later memory integration.

title: Define Mac mini allowlisted roots and path safety
description: Define the exact writable and readable roots for the home-mcp server on the Mac mini, and enforce path safety so the server cannot escape allowlisted directories.
design: Build a strict allowlist boundary first. No .. traversal, no symlink escape, no hidden-file access unless explicitly enabled, and no filesystem browsing outside configured roots. This is the foundation for every later tool.
acceptance_criteria: The repo documents the allowlisted roots and the server rejects any path outside them. Path normalization is tested, symlink escape attempts fail, and hidden or oversized reads are bounded by policy.

title: Build read-only file discovery and search tools
description: Add read-only file listing, file search, and file read tools scoped to allowlisted roots on the Mac mini.
design: The first tools should let AI discover files, search contents, and inspect notes and recipe documents without write access. Return structured JSON with path, file ID, snippets, and match reasons.
acceptance_criteria: The server can list files, search files, and read files within allowed roots. Results are structured, scoped, and logged, and attempts to search or read outside the configured roots are rejected.

title: Add recipe book directory and note write tools
description: Create a simple local recipe book directory on the Mac mini and add create-only or append-only Markdown note tools for recipes and related household/project notes.
design: Recipe content should be stored as hardcoded, inspectable Markdown notes first, not a complex database. Support create and append flows so AI can save recipe drafts, attempts, and notes safely without arbitrary overwrite or delete behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The server can create and append Markdown notes in the recipe book directory. File names are sanitized, writes are logged, overwrites are avoided by default, and the recipe note format is stable enough to surface later through the memory system.

title: Add audit logging and trace coverage for MCP calls
description: Record every home-mcp tool call with run IDs, inputs, outputs, and failure stages so the Mac mini surface is inspectable from the outside.
design: Every read and write tool should emit trace events and durable logs. Error localization should point to the stage, path, or tool that failed so the system is not a black box when ChatGPT or Codex calls it.
acceptance_criteria: Tool calls produce audit entries and trace artifacts. Failures identify a stage and source path or file ID, and the logs can be inspected later to reconstruct what the AI tried to do.

title: Add remote access transport and authentication
description: Make the Mac mini MCP server reachable to approved outside AI clients through a controlled tunnel or relay with authentication and explicit exposure boundaries.
design: Use a tunnel-based or relay-based transport instead of raw port forwarding. ChatGPT should be able to reach the service, but only through narrow authenticated endpoints and only for the approved tools.
acceptance_criteria: The server is reachable from an external client through the chosen transport. Access requires authentication or equivalent trust gating, and the exposure path is documented and reversible.

title: Bridge recipe book into the memory system
description: Expose the local recipe book directory to the existing memory system later so recipe notes can be searched and promoted alongside ChatGPT transcript memory.
design: Keep this as a later integration step. The recipe book should remain usable on its own first, then a bridge can ingest or index it into the memory stack once the file format and workflow are stable.
acceptance_criteria: A documented path exists for moving or indexing recipe book entries into the memory system later, without changing the primary recipe note workflow or weakening the Mac mini safety boundary.

title: Analyze user input over time
description: Track user prompt behavior over time: semantic density, length, topic distribution, and other metadata that can show how AI usage changes. Keep it separate from the recipe/MCP work for now.
acceptance_criteria:
Can report per-period averages for input length and semantic density.
Can cluster or summarize topics over time.
Can compare recent usage to historical baselines.
Can be added later without changing the current memory/recipe pipeline.

title: Expose memory system to ChatGPT
description: Make the existing local memory stack available to ChatGPT through the approved home-mcp/tunnel path, with narrow tools for read/search/review/promotion and traceable audit logs. Keep this separate from the recipe-book bridge so the memory integration can be built and verified independently.
acceptance_criteria: ChatGPT can reach the memory system through an approved MCP surface or bridge. The exposed tools are narrow, auditable, and role-scoped. Search/review/promote flows remain separate from raw data access. Trace logs show which memory action was invoked and where it failed if a request breaks.
